content.text:
Phase 10 can be a seed-only change. The current engine already runs filter, then transform, then an HTTP step, and a Discord incoming webhook returns 2xx for a `{ "content": "..." }` body. No engine, SSRF, runs API, or README change is required.

## What is already in place

Workflows are JSONB documents. `WorkflowRepository` can list, create, and replace a workflow. `replace` and `update` do not touch `triggerToken` or `triggerPath`. There is no demo-id column and no `scripts/` directory. `loadConfig` does not read a webhook URL. `ALLOW_PRIVATE_URLS` defaults to false. The HTTP step posts `step.url` as stored; it does not read an environment variable at execution time. Custom body strings are interpolated. Any HTTP 2xx, including Discord’s usual 204, is success.

The challenge sample is the right demo shape: two AND filter conditions (`type == lock.unlock` and `success == false`), then `default`, `template`, and `pick`. The sample HTTP body mode is `ctx`, aimed at `http://localhost:9000/alerts`. That body is not a Discord message. The seeded step has to send Discord’s `{ "content" }` shape instead. Playwright stays on the mock webhook and is not part of this phase.

## 1. Seed script location and command

Put the testable logic in the API workspace, where Prisma, `tsx`, and the repository already live:

- `apps/api/src/seed/demo-workflow.ts` — pure definition and upsert
- `apps/api/src/seed/seed-demo.ts` — CLI
- `apps/api/src/seed/demo-workflow.test.ts`

The approved plan’s `scripts/seed-demo.ts` would sit outside `apps/api` `rootDir`, so it would not be typechecked. The same command name is enough:

- `@kisi-workflow/api`: `"seed": "tsx src/seed/seed-demo.ts"`
- repo root: `"seed": "npm run seed -w @kisi-workflow/api"`

The CLI reads `process.env` only. It does not load dotenv and does not call `loadConfig`, so seeding does not require `PUBLIC_URL` or `DEMO_ACCESS_KEY`. Prisma already requires `DATABASE_URL`. The CLI prints the trigger path and whether the row was created or updated. It does not print the webhook URL.

## 2. How the demo workflow is identified

Identify it by the exact name `Demo unlock alert`. That name is unique in practice, fits the 100-character limit, and does not match the e2e workflow name `Unlock alerts`.

Lookup uses the existing `list()`:

- Keep rows whose `name` equals `Demo unlock alert`.
- If several match, update the earliest `createdAt`. Tie-break on `id` ascending.
- Do not delete the extras.

Renaming the workflow in the UI makes the next seed create a new row. That is the limit of name identity without a schema change. A fixed UUID would survive renames, but `WorkflowRepository.create` does not accept an id, so it is not proposed.

## 3. Demo workflow definition

Enabled, name `Demo unlock alert`. Steps are parsed with `WorkflowStepsSchema` before write.

1. **Filter** (AND, same as the challenge sample):
   - `type` `eq` `lock.unlock`
   - `success` `eq` `false`
2. **Transform**, in sample order:
   - `default` `actor_name` to `Unknown`
   - `template` `title` to `Event {{type}} by {{actor_name}}`
   - `pick` `uuid`, `type`, `success`, `severity`, `title`
3. **HTTP request**:
   - `POST`
   - `url`: the validated `DEMO_WEBHOOK_URL`
   - headers: `Content-Type: application/json` and `X-Workflow-Id: {{workflow_id}}`
   - body: `{ "mode": "custom", "json": { "content": "{{title}}" } }`
   - `timeoutMs`: 2000
   - `retries`: 3

`mode: "ctx"` would send the picked event object. Discord rejects that as an empty message. `content` is interpolated from `title` after the transform, so the posted message is `Event lock.unlock by Unknown` when `actor_name` is absent. `workflow_id` still comes from the existing template binding after `pick` drops it from `ctx`.

Smoke payload, for later production checks, not for this phase’s tests:

```json
{
  "uuid": "demo-event-1",
  "type": "lock.unlock",
  "success": false,
  "severity": "warning"
}
```

A matching event with `success: true`, or any other `type`, skips and does not call Discord.

## 4. How the Discord URL is supplied

`DEMO_WEBHOOK_URL` is read only by the seed CLI. It is written into the `http_request` step, which is the existing execution model. It is never hardcoded, never committed, and never given a `VITE_` name.

Reject the seed, with no write, unless the value is `https` and the host is `discord.com`, `discordapp.com`, `canary.discord.com`, or `ptb.discord.com`, with a path under `/api/webhooks/`. Validate with the shared `HttpOrHttpsUrlSchema` as well. Error text names the variable and the rule. It does not echo the value.

Add an empty `DEMO_WEBHOOK_URL=` entry to `apps/api/.env.example` and the root `.env.example`. Do not add it to `loadConfig` or `apps/web/.env.example`.

The editor will still show the URL after seed, because `GET /workflows` already returns `steps` and Monaco edits that document. There is no new frontend field or bundle variable. Hiding it would mean redacting steps in the API, which would also break editing that step. That is not part of this phase.

Production stays `ALLOW_PRIVATE_URLS=false`. A public `https://discord.com/...` URL already passes the current SSRF checks. The seed does not weaken those checks and does not call Discord.

## 5. Repeated runs

| Situation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| No row with that name | `WorkflowService.create` with `enabled: true`. Existing token-collision retry applies. |
| One or more rows with that name | `WorkflowService.put` on the earliest row: same name, `enabled: true`, steps rebuilt from the current env URL. |
| Row was disabled | Put turns it back on. |
| Other workflow names | Left untouched. |
| Invalid or missing URL | Throw before any create or update. |

`put` keeps `id`, `triggerToken`, and `triggerPath`. Every successful run rewrites steps, so rotating `DEMO_WEBHOOK_URL` and redeploying updates the stored URL without a new token. Two overlapping seeds can both insert if neither has committed yet. Render’s pre-deploy runs once, so that race is acceptable.

## 6. How deployment invokes it

Phase 10 does not add Render config or boot-time seeding. `server.ts` stays a listen path. Local `dev` does not seed.

Phase 12 should run this after migrations and before the process listens, as a Render pre-deploy command:

```bash
npm run prisma:migrate -w @kisi-workflow/api && npm run seed
```

That fails the deploy if `DEMO_WEBHOOK_URL` is missing, instead of crash-looping the web process. Expected production env: `DATABASE_URL` from Render Postgres, `PUBLIC_URL`, `NODE_ENV=production`, `ALLOW_PRIVATE_URLS=false`, `DEMO_WEBHOOK_URL`, and `DEMO_ACCESS_KEY` because `loadConfig` still requires it. `VITE_DEMO_ACCESS_KEY` remains the existing browser credential only.

The README stays the current install, test, and e2e commands.

## 7. Tests and verification

Vitest, in-memory repository, no Postgres and no `fetch`:

- Missing, blank, `http:`, non-Discord host, or non-webhook path creates nothing.
- First seed creates one enabled workflow whose steps match the definition above, with a 32-character hex token.
- Second seed with a different fixture URL updates that step URL, keeps `id` and `triggerToken`, and leaves the count at one.
- A disabled match is enabled again.
- A workflow with another name is unchanged.
- Two rows with the demo name: the earlier one is updated, no third row is created.

Fixture URL: `https://discord.com/api/webhooks/example/example`.

Verification when implementing: the new test file, `npm test -w @kisi-workflow/api`, and `npm run typecheck`. No e2e or live Discord call in this phase.

## 8. Application changes

Required:

- The seed module, CLI, tests, and `seed` scripts.
- Empty `DEMO_WEBHOOK_URL=` in the two `.env.example` files.

Not in this phase: Prisma schema, repository interface, engine, SSRF, `loadConfig`, routes, UI, runs API, Playwright, README, Dockerfile, or Render config.

content.text:
Phase 10 is implemented as a repeatable seed. The demo workflow is created or updated by name, the Discord URL is taken only from `DEMO_WEBHOOK_URL`, and an existing row keeps its id and trigger token.

`npm run seed` runs `apps/api/src/seed/seed-demo.ts`. It validates the webhook URL before any database call, then creates or updates the workflow named `Demo unlock alert`. The steps are the approved filter, transform, and Discord `POST` with `{ "content": "{{title}}" }`. A second run rewrites that row, including turning it back on, and leaves its `id`, `triggerToken`, and `triggerPath` in place. If several rows share the name, the earliest `createdAt` is updated, with the lowest `id` breaking a tie. The command prints `created /t/...` or `updated /t/...` and does not print the webhook URL. Any other failure is reported as `seed failed`.

## TDD result

- Behavior: idempotent seed of the enabled Discord demo workflow from `DEMO_WEBHOOK_URL`.
- Tests added: `apps/api/src/seed/demo-workflow.test.ts` (11 cases). They failed first because the module was missing, then passed after the implementation.
- Implementation: `apps/api/src/seed/demo-workflow.ts` and `apps/api/src/seed/seed-demo.ts`.
- Files changed:
  - `apps/api/src/seed/demo-workflow.ts`
  - `apps/api/src/seed/seed-demo.ts`
  - `apps/api/src/seed/demo-workflow.test.ts`
  - `apps/api/package.json`
  - `package.json`
  - `apps/api/.env.example`
  - `.env.example`
- Verification:
  - focused: `npm test -w @kisi-workflow/api -- src/seed/demo-workflow.test.ts` → pass (11)
  - suite: `npm test -w @kisi-workflow/api` → pass (132)
  - typecheck: `npm run typecheck` → pass
  - `git diff --check` → pass

Nothing was committed.

One test detail differs from using only `InMemoryWorkflowRepository`. Duplicate-name ordering needs fixed `createdAt` values and ids, which that repository assigns itself, so those two cases use a fixed in-memory repository in the test file. Create, update, token preservation, and unrelated workflows still go through `InMemoryWorkflowRepository`. No engine, SSRF, route, UI, schema, Playwright, README, or Render files were changed.
